item.title: Woman dies after collision between four vehicles in al Luqa
item.description: A woman involved in a collision between four vehicles at around 1pm on Triq al Qormi, al Luqa, was later pronounced dead in hospital. Police said initial investigations indicated that, for reasons still unknown, the collision occurred between the four vehicles, one of which was considerably larger than the others. More details are expected in the course of the investigation.

item.title: Record 16.6m wave between Malta and Sicily was highest ever in the Mediterranean
item.description: Research published in Nature by Maltese and Italian scientists found Storm Harry, which battered Malta in January, produced the highest wave ever documented in the Mediterranean, with a buoy between Malta and Sicily recording an individual wave of 16.6 metres. The Grand Harbour saw 0.85 square kilometres of flooding, with water reaching 2.9 metres above sea level at the Marsamxett Harbour entrance, and south-eastern Sicily was the most heavily impacted region, with more than seven kilometres of land flooded.

item.title: Garb residents oppose six-storey elderly care home on agricultural land
item.description: Residents in Garb are fighting a proposed care home for 48 elderly people after a Planning Authority case officer recommended approval. The local residents association says nearly 1,000 objections have been lodged across different versions of the plans, citing the buildings scale, its impact on the village character and encroachment into Outside Development Zone land. The case is due before the Planning Authority on 10 November.

item.title: Two-year suspended sentence for driver who killed horse-sulky rider
item.description: Gabriella Huhn Privitera was handed a two-year prison sentence suspended for four years after admitting the involuntary homicide of 66-year-old Joseph Camilleri, who was killed in a road accident on Triq ad Dingli in Rabat on 11 March 2022. She was acquitted of seriously injuring a second occupant of the carriage, of damaging the horse-drawn carriage and of negligent driving.

item.title: Malta has second-lowest household electricity prices in the EU
item.description: New Eurostat figures for the first half of 2026 show Maltese households paid an average of 0.13 per kWh, tying with Bulgaria and behind only Hungary at 0.11, against an EU average of 0.28. Adjusted for purchasing power, Malta came out cheapest in the EU at 13.8 per 100 kWh. EU-wide prices fell 2.2% over the period but remain well above pre-2022 energy crisis levels.

item.title: Warren Collection to cover up to 400 of work permit fees for foreign staff
item.description: The Maltese hotel group behind Park Heights in Msida and Eleven in Sliema said it will contribute up to 400 towards the additional work permit renewal costs faced by eligible third-country national employees, starting January 2027 when the Budget 2027 permit charges take effect. Ramla Bay Resort made a similar pledge over the weekend.

item.title: 3,057 students benefited from school uniform and stationery support schemes
item.description: Education Minister Byron Camilleri told Parliament that 2,631 students benefited from Scheme 9 and 426 from BM40 during the 2025-2026 school year, providing help with uniforms, basic stationery packs or extra-curricular activities for families facing financial hardship or at risk of social exclusion.

item.title: Family condemns acquittal in Lassana Cisse murder trial as police chief calls verdict demoralising
item.description: The cousin of Lassana Cisse, an Ivorian father of two shot dead in a racist drive-by attack in al Far in 2019, said the verdict acquitting former soldier Lorin Scicluna of the murder is not justice; it is total disregard for the value of human life. Survivor May Malimi, whom Scicluna drove into, said he was not happy with the not-guilty verdict. Police Commissioner Angelo Gaf called the 8-1 jury decision demoralising, while Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield said such verdicts leave a bad taste but that the police form only one part of the wider judicial system. Scicluna was convicted of grievous bodily harm and of driving without a number plate; sentencing submissions are scheduled for Wednesday. Sciclunas defence was also offered a 30-year plea bargain days before trial, which he refused.

item.title: Ombudsman warns stop-gap homeless measures do not address the root causes
item.description: Parliamentary Ombudsman Joseph Zammit McKeon said police interventions and temporary shelters for people sleeping rough are provisional measures that do not address the real causes of the accommodation and security problem. Referring to a person found lying in a St Anne Street subway in Floriana, he stressed that success should not be measured by moving people from the streets, but by there being fewer people sleeping rough.

item.title: Court finds no medical negligence in magistrates death after Mater Dei operation
item.description: The family of magistrate Joseph Cassar, who died on 2 May 2017 after an angioplasty at Mater Dei Hospital, lost a medical negligence claim in the First Hall Civil Court. Judge Rachel Montebello ruled that the medical team followed accepted professional standards and that the death resulted from a rare two-centimetre tear in the femoral artery with internal bleeding, compounded by pre-existing heart disease. The family was ordered to bear legal costs.

item.title: Minister and police commissioner defend the force after a string of acquittals
item.description: Speaking at the Ta Kandja Police Academy, Glenn Bedingfield said no one is perfect and that police mistakes happen but are not intentional, after journalists raised investigative errors in the Yorgen Fenech case, the Keith Schembri search and the Raymond Fenech and Michael Stivala cases. Commissioner Angelo Gaf said every mistake must be examined carefully and that the Professional Standards Office investigates where wrongdoing is identified, with disciplinary action to follow.

item.title: University of Malta research maps memory effect in quantum communication links
item.description: University of Malta researchers showed that slight mistiming in when a receiver stores a quantum message leaves traces inside the channel, so the quality of each subsequent communication degrades with every use. The effect also limits how much entanglement a channel can carry, a resource central to quantum advantage and many quantum technologies.

item.title: Floriana mayor warns boutique hotel conversions could cost the town its community
item.description: Mayor Nigel Holland said the locality could end up without a community as large residences are converted into boutique hotels and Airbnb short-lets, following an application to turn the former Floriana power station into a boutique hotel. Maltese residents in the town have fallen from 1,959 in 2012 to 1,566 in 2024.

item.title: Budget 2027 non-EU worker measures face legal challenge; refugees exempt
item.description: Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield confirmed that refugees and persons with subsidiary or temporary humanitarian protection will keep free public transport and free childcare, despite the Budget 2027 withdrawal of those benefits for third-country nationals. The wider package higher work permit fees, an 400 annual infrastructure contribution and charges for driving ones own car is widely expected to be challenged, with Aditus Foundation head Neil Falzon citing the EU Single Permit Directive on equal access to goods and services. Malta also missed the May 2026 deadline to transpose the recast directive and has received a formal notice from the European Commission.

item.title: Libya requests extradition of Lilu King; Malta seeks guarantees before deciding
item.description: Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield said Libya submitted a written request in September for the extradition of Mohamed Ali Elmushraty, better known as Lilu King, who faces drug trafficking and homicide charges at home. Maltese authorities are evaluating the request, but Bedingfield said he told the Libyan Attorney General during a September visit to Tripoli that guarantees are required under Maltese law and the European Convention on Human Rights before any decision. Elmushraty was stripped of refugee status in September and is in pre-trial detention over separate organised crime and money laundering proceedings.

item.title: Force 7 winds and showers to batter Malta from this evening
item.description: The Malta Meteorological Office forecasts west-northwesterly winds of Force 5 to 6 during Monday, strengthening to Force 6 to 7 overnight with isolated showers. Near-gale Force 7 conditions correspond to speeds of roughly 50 to 61 km/h. Maximum temperatures of 19C are expected, dropping to 15C overnight, with winds persisting into Tuesday.

item.title: Labour MP defends embryo screening expansion against disability sector concerns
item.description: Labour MP Romilda Zarb, the mother of a son with Down syndrome, said extending pre-implantation genetic testing for monogenic disorders to 17 further conditions does not conflict with disability rights. The Malta Federation of Organisations of Persons with Disability had warned the expansion risks suggesting some lives are worth more than others. Zarb said the screening is only offered to couples already going through IVF with serious hereditary conditions, and said she speaks on it because she knows some parents would otherwise seek it abroad.

item.title: Former housing minister Galdes lands new government job two days after resigning
item.description: Roderick Galdes was given a managerial role at the National Skills Council just two days after resigning from Cabinet over pressure concerning his dealings with contractors. Freedom of information documents show he signed the contract on 26 January, with a financial package worth over 60,000 including a car allowance and a 10% responsibility allowance. Galdes denies the post is compensation for his resignation.

item.title: Property prices cushion falling sales as rents keep rising
item.description: The Central Bank of Maltas Q3 2026 Business Dialogue report finds demand still exceeds supply in both sales and rentals, but weakening affordability is pushing fewer sales through. Higher prices are offsetting lower transaction volumes, while rental demand continues to push rents upwards and summer conversions to tourist-lets are tightening the long-term rental market.

item.title: Planning Authority approves Tarxien block over heritage objections
item.description: The Planning Commission approved the demolition of an existing dwelling in Tarxiens urban conservation area and its replacement with 10 apartments, despite objections from the local council, the heritage watchdog and residents. The scheme spans Triq Paola and Triq Lanzon and includes basement excavation for six car garages, with Second World War air-raid shelters at both ends of the bordering streets.
